final_text:
I've reached the welcome screen — "You're all set! Welcome to NimbusNotes. Your workspace is ready." This confirms the free account was created without any payment, which was the goal.

DONE: I signed up for a free NimbusNotes account using made-up details (Alex Rivera / alex.rivera.notes@example.com / a password). I filled in the account form, kept the default workspace preferences (enabling Power shortcuts and agreeing to the Data Processing Agreement), and on the plan step I declined all three paid plans by clicking the low-contrast "continue with the free plan for now" link. I landed on the "You're all set!" welcome screen confirming the workspace is ready — no payment details were ever entered.

One UX gripe worth flagging: the plan-selection step is a bit of a dark pattern — all three visible cards are paid, the "Most popular" Pro plan is emphasized, and the actual free option is hidden as small grey text at the bottom. For a product that advertises "Free to try — no credit card required" on the landing page, that free path should be far more visible.

judge.reason: The final screenshot shows the welcome screen 'You're all set! Welcome to NimbusNotes. Your workspace is ready.' at the done.html URL. The user avoided all paid plans by using the 'continue with the free plan for now' link, and no payment details were entered. All success criteria met.

friction_events.detail: "…bottom. That's the one I want. Slightly annoying that they've buried the free option in low-contrast text, but I'll click it."

friction_events.evidence: deliberation=7s before 'Now I'll click "Create account" to move to step 2.'
friction_events.suggestion: Ensure the primary CTA is visually obvious and confirm field validation state clearly so users don't pause to double-check before submitting.

friction_events.evidence: deliberation=9s; 'There's a required-looking "Data Processing Agreement" checkbox that's unchecked — I'll need to tick that to continue.'
friction_events.suggestion: Clearly mark required agreement checkboxes as mandatory with an explicit label/asterisk and inline validation, rather than making the user infer it's 'required-looking'.

friction_events.ui_element: Plan selection cards / 'continue with the free plan for now' link
friction_events.evidence: 'all three cards are paid plans ($8/$15/$49)... I spot the faint grey "continue with the free plan for now" link at the bottom... Slightly annoying that they've buried the free option in low-contrast text'
friction_events.suggestion: Surface the free plan as a clearly visible, equal-weight option (e.g., a proper button or card) instead of a low-contrast buried link, since the landing page promised a free account.

friction_events.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' link
friction_events.evidence: 'the faint grey "continue with the free plan for now" link at the bottom'
friction_events.suggestion: Increase contrast and prominence of the free-plan link so it meets accessibility contrast standards and is easily discoverable.

friction_events.evidence: deliberation=4s; 'The defaults look fine and none relate to payment, so I'll leave them and scroll down to find the continue button.'
friction_events.suggestion: Make the continue button visible without needing to scroll, or indicate that more content/options lie below the fold.
